prompt_verbatim:
Create a NEW production animation sprite sheet based closely on the supplied reference art. This is an extension of an existing game character, not a redesign. EXACT layout: FOUR equal-width columns and TWO equal-height rows, EIGHT isolated complete character poses, ordered left to right, no ninth pose. Transparent RGBA background with no opaque backdrop, no shadows outside the body, no grid lines, labels, text, effects, sparks, particles, blood or motion trails. The sheet is a landscape 2:1 canvas with square cells, equal generous transparent padding per cell. Keep matching scale, camera, anatomy, materials, lighting and contour treatment between every frame. Face RIGHT in all frames including prone poses. Same upper-left soft light and bright broad material planes, dark joints; no neon or glossy plastic. These are actual anatomical redraws: joint angles, head relative to torso, limb contact positions, folded limbs and silhouette visibly change. Do NOT create copies differing only in global rotation, translation, stretch, tint or alpha. Every complete body fits inside its own cell without touching borders or neighbouring bodies. Row one is four hurt/recovery keyframes, row two is four death keyframes. Last death frame is a clearly dead but intact body suitable to remain visible on the floor indefinitely; no explosion, dissolution, skeleton or disappearance. Last frame keeps readable midtones with extinguished eye.

REFERENCE: the desired character is ONLY the small hovering contraption in the LOWER-RIGHT of the supplied source atlas, approximately x935 y570 width580 height445 in a 1536x1024 image. Ignore completely the wagon top-left, wheel top-right, and projectile bottom-left. Preserve this exact legacy flying machine: compact round rough off-white limestone-and-moss ball held in warm copper/brass curved bands and rivets, round orange lens eye on front-left of source which should be shown on the RIGHT-facing front in new sheet, small hanging brass bells, central brass neck above ball, and two long flat pointed moss-green leaf rotor blades on top. It has ONE two-blade leaf rotor, not insect wings. Warm hand-drawn illustrated outline and textured materials, matching reference, not pixel art redesign or robotic sci-fi. TOP ROW: H1 lens/front pitches back slightly, one hanging bell lags outward and rotor linkage bends; H2 two leaf blades become asymmetrically tilted, neck hunches visibly and bells fold toward body; H3 neck straightens and rotor blades recover at different angles, bell swings inward; H4 stable original hovering ready arrangement with horizontal opposed leaf rotor and lit orange eye. BOTTOM ROW: D1 eye dims and rotor hub sags, one leaf blade droops; D2 neck linkage folds forward and blades angle down independently, bells collapse toward shell as body loses lift; D3 ball body lies on its side with folded neck, both leaf rotor blades collapsed alongside body and a hanging bell resting against shell; D4 intact stable dead side-lying ball machine on floor, extinguished dark lens, folded rotor and neck along its side instead of airborne horizontal active rotor, stone and brass materials still readable, bells at rest. Death is articulated mechanical collapse, NOT a flying ball merely globally rotated. No detached debris, no added insect legs, no wings, no flames.
